Sales grew, but this stock still crashed sixteen percent. You're reading results wrong.
Last Friday, Intellect Design fell sixteen percent to a fifty two week low. The same day, Laurus Labs jumped seven percent to a record high.
One makes bank software, one makes medicines. Both grew sales last quarter. So why cheer one, and dump the other?
Most people think sales up means stock up. That's the myth. But wait till you see the profit line.
Laurus. Revenue up thirty three percent. Profit up one hundred twenty six percent, to four hundred forty one crore. Margins jumped from twenty six to thirty four percent.
Intellect. Income up eleven percent, but profit barely moved, one hundred four crore versus one hundred two, and revenue missed expectations.
But a record high has risk too. Laurus is up about two and a half times in a year, and Kotak still rates it sell. High expectations are easy to disappoint.
So here's the rule. Stocks don't move on good news. They move on surprise. Check three things. Profit growth, margins, and what the market expected.
